chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abdul Malik al-Qummi, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The one in Ihram performs ablution, then covers his face with a handkerchief, concealing it entirely.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person in Ihram to cover their face with a cloth?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of covering the face with a cloth like a handkerchief during Ihram, clarifying that such an act does not constitute a violation requiring expiation. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between covering the face (which is generally permissible) and covering the head (which is prohibited), highlighting the practical flexibility allowed for pilgrims in maintaining their sacred state. The chain of transmission through Abd al-Malik al-Qummi underscores the reliability of this legal precedent within the Usuli tradition.
